tool_input.command: find / -path "*/node_modules/@guren/core*" -maxdepth 6 -type d 2>/dev/null | head; echo ---; find / -path "*/node_modules/@guren/cli*" -maxdepth 6 -type d 2>/dev/null | head

cat > /tmp/zodcheck.mjs << 'EOF'
import { z } from 'zod'
const RegisterSchema = z.object({
  name: z.string(),
  password: z.string(),
  passwordConfirmation: z.string(),
}).refine((data) => data.password === data.passwordConfirmation, { message: 'no match', path: ['passwordConfirmation'] })
console.log(RegisterSchema._def.type)
console.log(Object.keys(RegisterSchema._def))
console.log(RegisterSchema._zod?.def?.type)
EOF
bun /tmp/zodcheck.mjs
git stash && bun test 2>&1 | tail -20; git stash pop

cp resources/js/pages/auth/Register.tsx /tmp/Register.tsx.bak
sed -i '' 's/passwordConfirmation/passwordConfirmatoin/g' resources/js/pages/auth/Register.tsx
bun run typecheck 2>&1 | tail -40

result: I annotated `routes/auth.ts` to attach `RegisterSchema` (the existing server-side Zod schema, unchanged) as the `body` for `register.store`, then ran `bun run codegen` to regenerate `.guren/api-client.gen.ts` (and the reflected `.guren/pages.gen.ts`) so `ApiRoutes['register.store']['body']` now carries the server's exact field shape. `resources/js/pages/auth/Register.tsx` was updated to derive `RegisterFormData` from that generated type (instead of a hand-written duplicate), type the `errors` prop from `keyof RegisterFormData`, and post via `route('register.store')` from the generated route helper instead of a hard-coded `/register` string — mirroring the pattern already used by the post editor's `New.tsx`/`Edit.tsx`. I verified by temporarily renaming every `passwordConfirmation` occurrence in the file to a misspelling (typecheck failed at all four usage sites) and by pointing the submit at `route('register.stor')` (typecheck failed there too), then restored the correct file. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass on the final result, and no runtime behavior (route name, path, field names, validation rules) changed.
